claims.text: Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V is a Group IV-V transition-metal refractory high-entropy alloy system.
The Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V alloy can be fabricated by LPBF using pre-alloyed powders.
The proposed sequence is hot rolling at 1200 °C with 80% reduction, cold rolling at 25 °C with 75% reduction, annealing at 900 °C for 5 minutes, and aging at 650 °C for 20 hours.
This thermo-mechanical sequence will induce stepwise coherent δ-lamella and γ″-particle precipitation in LPBF Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V.
The initial LPBF Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The initial LPBF alloy has W-enriched grains and V depletion.
The initial LPBF alloy contains approximately 500 nm subgrains.
Spherical V-rich precipitates occur at boundaries in the initial LPBF alloy.
The as-printed Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V alloy contains appreciable porosity.
Brittleness in the initial alloy is caused by interstitial impurities and rapid-solidification defects.
Processing in high-purity argon minimizes interstitial contamination.
The target microstructure contains approximately 40 nm-wide coherent δ-lamellae with a D0a structure.
The target microstructure contains approximately 10 nm spheroidal coherent γ″ particles with a D022 structure.
Coherent δ and γ″ interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations.
The coherent precipitates prevent premature crack initiation associated with interstitial impurities and grain-boundary segregation.
Lamellar boundaries and particle pinning provide synergistic strengthening while retaining ductility through strain hardening.
The processed alloy will exceed 2.0 GPa ultimate tensile strength and 10% tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
The processed alloy will retain more than 1.0 GPa yield strength at 800 °C.
The as-printed LPBF Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V baseline has 95% density.
The as-printed baseline has 1391 MPa compressive strength and brittle failure associated with porosity and unmelted particles.

contradictions.description: The route is repeatedly called 'dual-stage aging,' but the specified schedule contains one short anneal at 900 °C and only one explicit aging treatment at 650 °C; it does not specify two aging stages.

The prediction requires UTS above 2.0 GPa and ductility above 10%, whereas the mechanical falsification thresholds are only UTS below 1.5 GPa or elongation below 5%. Results between these thresholds would violate the prediction without satisfying the stated mechanical falsification rule.
